:::{#exm-flat-point}
#### Flat points, and a point that is not one

- $f(w) = w^3$ has $f'(w) = 3w^2$,
  which is $0$ at $w = 0$,
  so $0$ is a flat point.
  Yet $f(0) = 0$ is neither the [minimum](algebra.qmd#def-minimum)
  nor the [maximum](algebra.qmd#def-maximum)
  of the [values](functions.qmd#def-value) $f$ takes on any [open interval](sets.qmd#def-open-interval) around $0$:
  $f(w) < 0$ for $w < 0$,
  and $f(w) > 0$ for $w > 0$.
- $h(w) = w^2$ has $h'(1) = 2 \ne 0$,
  so $1$ is not a flat point.

:::
